title: Adaptive prefill and staged-throttle recovery playbook for hosted GPU saturation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up and action plan after a hosted GPU pool saturation event that caused long queue build-up and aggressive throttling. This ticket captures analysis, runbook updates, short-term mitigations, and longer-term engineering changes intended to reduce recurrence and shorten recovery time. Goals: reduce queue amplification, improve tenant fairness during spikes, and enable rapid automated recovery without manual priming.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-27 a single tenant workload with large batched image-to-text jobs and frequent long-sequence text completions triggered disproportionate KV-cache growth and sequence-length skew. Autoscaler prewarm heuristics under-provisioned slots for long sequences; prefetch combined with tenant reservation decay allowed slot leaks. The result was sustained GPU pool saturation for ~2.5 hours, elevated 429/503 errors for multi-tenant hosted API customers, and manual intervention to drain and re-prime pools.
timeline: 2026-02-27 02:12 UTC: anomalous traffic spike detected for tenant T-714; sequence length median jumped x3
2026-02-27 02:20 UTC: pooled KV cache for pool G-03 exceeded expected per-tenant allocation, eviction pressure increased
2026-02-27 02:35 UTC: prefetch coordinator started aggressive warmups causing slot-owning to persist beyond expected TTL
2026-02-27 03:05 UTC: autoscaler delayed additional nodes due to hysteresis and misread short-window throughput; queue length increased rapidly
2026-02-27 03:40 UTC: first customer-facing rate-limits applied; 429s observed across several tenants
2026-02-27 04:10 UTC: on-call runbook executed: staged throttle, soft-eviction of highest-memory tenants, manual priming of spare nodes
2026-02-27 04:45 UTC: normal traffic rerouted and pool pressure decreased; full recovery at 05:35 UTC
root_cause: Interacting failures between prefetch/prefill logic, per-tenant KV-cache accounting, and autoscaler hysteresis. The prefill algorithm did not account for sequence-length distribution and KV cache residency; long-sequence requests held slots longer than the autoscaler window expected, which prevented fast autoscale and caused queue amplification. Additionally, no automated tenant fairness score existed to guide soft-eviction or staged throttles, so manual intervention was required.
mitigation_taken: Applied emergency staged throttle thresholds to reduce new admission for best-effort tenants
Soft-evicted top 3 KV cache consumers in pool G-03 to reclaim working set
Manually primed 4 nodes in adjacent region and temporarily increased prewarm concurrency
Updated post-incident alert to include per-tenant KV cache usage and sequence-length percentiles
action_items: (1) Build adaptive-prefill algorithm that weights prewarm credits by tenant fairness score and sequence-length percentiles — owner: Lucas Chen — estimate: 8 — due: 2026-03-26
(2) Implement sequence-length-aware slot packing: prefer co-packing short sequences and limit long-seq concurrency per-slot — owner: Priya Singh — estimate: 5 — due: 2026-04-02
(3) Per-tenant KV cache accounting + soft-eviction policy (LRU by tenant segment) and eviction telemetry — owner: Ethan Morales — estimate: 5 — due: 2026-03-19
(4) Autoscaler hysteresis tweak and fast-path for sustained long-sequence load (reduce scale window when median sequence length > threshold) — owner: Leila Romero — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-12

(5) Automated staged-throttle runbook: detect KV-pollution, compute tenant fairness score, apply graduated admission caps and fallback routing — owner: SRE team (oncall) — estimate: 5 — due: 2026-03-20
(6) Create a synthetic tenant stress test and add to continuous chaos suite to validate runbook and prefill behavior — owner: QA/Perf — estimate: 4 — due: 2026-04-09
(7) Dashboard and alerting: new panels for per-pool, per-tenant KV residency, sequence-length heatmap, and prefill pressure metric — owner: Observability — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-12
(8) Customer communications template and incident-summary automation for tenants affected by capacity events — owner: Customer Ops — estimate: 2 — due: 2026-03-05
followups: Measure impact of adaptive-prefill on cost-per-token and cold-start latency in A/B canary (target: no >10% median latency regression)
Run post-deploy chaos for 3 weeks to validate non-regression for prefill and eviction policies
Add regression alert rule to detect sudden increase in average slot hold-time per tenant
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive-prefill prototype deployed to canary and shows reduction in queue amplification in synthetic test by >=50%
Per-tenant KV residency telemetry available for all hosted pools
Automated staged-throttle runbook triggers reliably in the chaos test and execution completes without manual intervention
No customer-facing error rate regression in canary (429/503 not increased)
Documentation and customer communication templates reviewed by Customer Ops
